article.headline: A Plant-Growing SVG Test Splits Two Frontier AI Models
article.lede: Dev Ed (Eduard Cîrstea), a front-end educator with roughly 800,000 YouTube subscribers, asked two current flagship AI models to build a looping plant-growth animation in a single HTML file — no libraries — as the opening shot of a nine-part informal comparison. The task demands spatial reasoning, physics-feel animation, and clean SVG code simultaneously, making it a harder creative proxy than standard coding benchmarks.
article.body:
Anthropic released **Claude Opus 4.6** on February 5, 2026 — its most capable coding model at launch, priced at $5 per million input tokens and carrying a one-million-token *context window*. OpenAI followed with **GPT-5.4** on March 5, 2026; the “High” in the poster’s label refers not to a product tier but to a *reasoning effort level*, a parameter that instructs the model to spend more internal computation — burning additional *chain-of-thought* tokens before returning an answer — at the same base rate of $2.50 per million input tokens. At those sticker prices, Opus 4.6 is indeed roughly twice as expensive per token as GPT-5.4 Standard.

The prompt is a genuinely demanding creative test. *SVG* — Scalable Vector Graphics, an XML-based format for 2D vector images that runs natively in browsers — requires strict syntax: malformed tags silently fail to render. A plant-growth animation layered on top adds path geometry for organic shapes, *CSS keyframe* sequences for timing and easing, and aesthetic judgment to make stems and leaves feel naturally springy rather than mechanically stiff. There is no canonical correct answer and no training example to recall; the model must compose novel geometry from scratch. The instruction “seamlessly loops forever” raises the difficulty further, requiring the model to construct an invisible restart rather than a visible fade or cut.

On aesthetic grounds, Cîrstea preferred GPT-5.4: its leaf physics were “super cool” and the loop was seamless. Opus 4.6’s plant simply faded out — a valid animation strategy, but one that sidesteps the harder problem of an invisible restart. Speed felt comparable. Third-party comparisons from the same period broadly echo a similar split: Opus 4.6 tends to produce more syntactically precise CSS animations, while GPT-5.4 shows an edge on visual execution and creative polish.

Some caveats apply. This is the first of a nine-part series — Cîrstea’s own “1/9” tag — so the final picture may shift as different task types are tested. The cost claim also warrants scrutiny: “half cheaper” holds at base per-token rates, but GPT-5.4 at “High” reasoning effort burns substantially more tokens internally than a standard request; third-party estimates put the effective cost multiplier at 1.5× to 5× standard, which can narrow the apparent gap considerably depending on how long the model’s reasoning chain runs.

concepts.definition: The maximum amount of text — measured in tokens — that a language model can process in a single request. A 1-million-token context window allows a model to consider roughly 750,000 words of input at once, enabling it to work across very large codebases or documents without losing earlier context.

A parameter in OpenAI’s GPT-5 API that controls how much internal chain-of-thought computation the model performs before returning an answer. Higher effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh) instruct the model to think longer, burning more tokens in the process and increasing both latency and effective cost per task.

A technique in which a language model generates intermediate reasoning steps — often hidden from the user — before producing its final answer. Models that reason via chain-of-thought tend to perform better on complex multi-step problems, but the extra tokens consumed add to cost and latency.

Scalable Vector Graphics — an XML-based format for describing 2D graphics that renders natively in web browsers. Because SVG defines shapes mathematically rather than as pixels, images scale without distortion; however, the syntax is strict and malformed tags typically cause silent rendering failures.

A CSS animation primitive that defines the style of an element at specific moments in an animation sequence. Developers specify keyframes at percentage intervals and the browser interpolates transitions between them, controlling movement, opacity, and visual transforms over time.

article.fact_check: The claim that GPT-5.4 was “half cheaper than Opus” is directionally accurate at base API rates: GPT-5.4 Standard costs $2.50 per million input tokens versus $5.00 for Opus 4.6, a 2× difference. However, GPT-5.4 at “High” reasoning effort consumes substantially more tokens internally before returning a response; at high effort, the effective per-task cost can be 1.5× to 5× that of a standard request, potentially closing the cost gap significantly. The claim is not wrong, but it compares sticker prices rather than effective task costs at the effort level actually used.
article.thread_summary: This tweet is the first in a nine-part series comparing Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 on different coding and creative tasks. Initial impressions from this plant-animation test favor GPT-5.4 on design quality and price, with speed described as comparable. The remaining eight tests had not been published at the time this brief was written.

He shares tutorials, project walkthroughs, and insights on modern web technologies. His engaging teaching style has attracted a large following of aspiring developers.
